patch.objective: Databases versus data warehouses versus data lakes, and what each is for

sources.cite: Google Cloud, Cloud Digital Leader exam guide
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Six sections of about 16-17% each: Digital Transformation with Google Cloud; Exploring Data Transformation with Google Cloud; Innovating with Google Cloud Artificial Intelligence; Modernize Infrastructure and Applications with Google Cloud; Trust and Security with Google Cloud; Scaling with Google Cloud Operations. Quoted: 1.2.e 'Discuss how Google Cloud supports digital transformation with global infrastructure and data centers connected by a fast, reliable network'; 2.1.b 'Differentiate between basic data management concepts, in particular: databases; data warehouses; data lakes'; 2.3.c 'Describe how streaming analytics in real time makes data more useful and generates business value'; 3.1.e 'Explain why high-quality, accurate data is essential for successful ML models'; 4.1.b 'Define the main cloud migration terms, including: workload; retire; retain; rehost; lift and shift; replatform; move and improve; refactor; reimagine'. The course seed's section weights (18/18/18/18/18/10) differ from the guide's (to reconcile).

sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL: Replication lag
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: causes include an undersized replica, 'long-running replica queries' that block replay, and an overloaded replica; metrics replica_lag and network_lag ('If network_lag is negligible but replica_lag is high, the replica is the bottleneck'); fixes: right-size the replica, tune max_standby_streaming_delay (about 30-60 seconds) and check pg_stat_database_conflicts, 'Use different replicas for OLTP and OLAP'. That promoting a replica stops replication for good is from memory of the 'Promote replicas' page (to verify).
